Option 1: "گر به فسون زنده کرد مرده مسیحا - جز سخن خوب نیست سوی من افسون"  
The first line says something like "If the fathom (afsoun) brought the dead Messiah back to life," and the second line is "Nothing but good words is the way to me, fathom." The key elements here are the use of "afsoun" (which might be a poetic term) and the idea that good words can revive someone, even the Messiah. It seems to suggest that words have the power to bring life or revival, possibly in a spiritual or metaphorical sense.

Option 2: "مرده بودم به سخن های تو گشتم زنده - خفته بودم صفت حسن تو بیدارم کرد"  
This translates to "I was dead, by your words I became alive; I was asleep, the beauty of your traits made me awake." Here, the speaker is emphasizing that the beloved's words and their virtues (صفت حسن) have a life-giving and awakening effect. The theme is about the transformative power of the beloved's words and qualities.

Option 3: "سخن عشق کند در دل افسرده اثر - مرده در گور اگر زنده به تلقین گردد"  
The first part is "The words of love may have an effect on a sorrowful heart," and the second part is "If the dead in the grave is revived through teaching (taleqin)." This seems to be about the power of love's words to affect even a deeply sad heart and the idea that the dead can be spiritually revived through teachings. The mention of "تلقین" (taleqin) might refer to reciting verses to the dead, a Sufi practice. So the theme here is the spiritual revival through words of love or teachings.

It might be saying that those who focus on words are the dead (maybe spiritually dead), and the others (the beloved or the divine) are the living. The theme here is contrasting the speaker's state as dead versus the beloved's as alive, possibly due to their connection with words or truth.
